"""Pivot / unpivot round-trip helpers for a long-format metrics table.

Long schema:  region | month | metric | value
Wide schema:  region | month | revenue | units

Absence semantics: a (region, month, metric) combination that is missing in
the long frame stays missing after the round trip -- it never reappears as a
row holding a null value.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import polars as pl

KEY_COLS = ["region", "month"]
METRICS = ["revenue", "units"]

LONG_SCHEMA = {"region": pl.String, "month": pl.String, "metric": pl.String, "value": pl.Float64}


def canonical_long(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Canonical long form: exact column order, deduplicated keys, sorted."""
    return (
        df.select(KEY_COLS + ["metric", "value"])
        .unique(subset=KEY_COLS + ["metric"], keep="first")
        .sort(KEY_COLS + ["metric"])
    )


def pivot_wide(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Long -> wide: one row per (region, month) with revenue and units columns.

    Duplicated keys are collapsed deterministically (first value wins).
    """
    return (
        df.group_by(KEY_COLS)
        .agg(pl.col("value").first())
        .pivot(on="metric", index=KEY_COLS, values="value")
        .select(KEY_COLS + METRICS)
        .sort(KEY_COLS)
    )


def unpivot_long(wide: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Wide -> long: inverse of :func:`pivot_wide`.

    Null cells (i.e. metric combinations absent from the source long data)
    are dropped, so absence round-trips as an absent row rather than a
    null-valued row.
    """
    return (
        wide.unpivot(index=KEY_COLS, on=METRICS, variable_name="metric", value_name="value")
        .select(KEY_COLS + ["metric", "value"])
        .filter(pl.col("value").is_not_null())
        .sort(KEY_COLS + ["metric"])
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools

import polars as pl
import pytest

from transform import (
    KEY_COLS,
    METRICS,
    LONG_SCHEMA,
    canonical_long,
    pivot_wide,
    unpivot_long,
)

REGIONS = ["north", "south", "west"]
MONTHS = [f"2024-{m:02d}" for m in range(1, 7)]


def _base_rows() -> itertools.chain[tuple[str, str, str, float]]:
    """Deterministic generator over the full 3 x 6 x 2 key grid."""
    rows = []
    for i, (region, month) in enumerate(itertools.product(REGIONS, MONTHS)):
        rows.append((region, month, "revenue", 1000.0 + 10 * i))
        rows.append((region, month, "units", 50.0 + i))
    return itertools.chain(rows)


@pytest.fixture
def long_df() -> pl.DataFrame:
    # 90 rows: the 36-key grid cycled 2.5x (duplicate keys carry identical
    # values, so pivot_wide's first-wins aggregation stays deterministic).
    rows = list(itertools.islice(_base_rows(), 90))
    assert len(rows) == 90
    return pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=LONG_SCHEMA, orient="row")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- round trip


def test_fixture_shape_and_grid(long_df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
    assert long_df.height == 90
    assert long_df.columns == ["region", "month", "metric", "value"]
    assert set(long_df["region"].unique()) == set(REGIONS)
    assert sorted(long_df["month"].unique()) == MONTHS
    assert set(long_df["metric"].unique()) == set(METRICS)


def test_round_trip_frame_equal(long_df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
    round_tripped = unpivot_long(pivot_wide(long_df))
    expected = canonical_long(long_df)

    assert round_tripped.columns == expected.columns  # column order pinned
    assert round_tripped.shape == expected.shape
    assert round_tripped.frame_equal(expected)  # exact values, order included


# ------------------------------------------------------ point checks on wide


def test_pivot_wide_point_assertions(long_df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
    wide = pivot_wide(long_df)

    # One row per (region, month): 3 regions x 6 months.
    assert wide.shape == (18, 4)
    assert wide.columns == ["region", "month", "revenue", "units"]

    # Spot-check known cells: north/2024-01 is grid position i=0,
    # west/2024-06 is i=17.
    north_jan = wide.filter(region="north", month="2024-01")
    assert north_jan["revenue"][0] == 1000.0
    assert north_jan["units"][0] == 50.0

    west_jun = wide.filter(region="west", month="2024-06")
    assert west_jun["revenue"][0] == 1170.0
    assert west_jun["units"][0] == 67.0


# ------------------------------------------- tricky case: missing combination


@pytest.fixture
def long_missing_one_cell(long_df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Same data but (south, 2024-03, units) removed from the long frame."""
    return long_df.filter(
        ~((pl.col("region") == "south") & (pl.col("month") == "2024-03") & (pl.col("metric") == "units"))
    )


def test_missing_combination_is_absent_not_null(
    long_missing_one_cell: pl.DataFrame,
) -> None:
    wide = pivot_wide(long_missing_one_cell)

    # Only one long row was dropped, so south/2024-03 still exists via its
    # revenue cell -- but the wide frame now holds exactly 17 fully-populated
    # rows and one partially populated one. No fabricated rows appear.
    assert wide.height == 18
    assert wide.drop_nulls().height == 17

    partial = wide.filter(region="south", month="2024-03")
    assert partial.height == 1
    assert partial["revenue"][0] == 1130.0  # grid position i=13
    assert partial["units"][0] is None

    # The round trip restores absence: no (south, 2024-03, units) row comes
    # back, and certainly none carrying a null value.
    rt = unpivot_long(wide)
    assert rt.height == 35
    resurrected = rt.filter(
        (pl.col("region") == "south")
        & (pl.col("month") == "2024-03")
        & (pl.col("metric") == "units")
    )
    assert resurrected.height == 0
    assert rt.filter(pl.col("value").is_null()).height == 0

    # And the round trip still matches the canonical input exactly.
    assert rt.frame_equal(canonical_long(long_missing_one_cell))
